outcome: The audit of 0.21.0..master fixed 54 of the 55 high and medium defects it confirmed, plus two found in its completion review, two in its closing review and one exposed by the later NCM zero-copy receive on master (dwc2 DMA OUT buffers are now cleaned from the D-cache before DMA): control-request direction checks (an OUT GET_DESCRIPTOR could write into the descriptor buffer), enumeration paths that stranded later devices, class parser bounds and lifecycle bugs, and controller toggle, stall, halt and IRQ-state bugs across dwc2, ehci, ip3516, wch, rusb2, rp2, fsdev, musb, ohci and max3421. Babysitting the PR merged the rp2 host rework from master and fixed the review findings on it, among them the non-buffered vendor OUT re-arm length when a bulk IN follows, and host stack and MAX3421 cleanup when controller init fails. API consequences of the range: tud_task_ext()/tuh_task_ext() and tud_task()/tuh_task() now return bool, with new tud_task_stop()/tuh_task_stop(); the obsolete vendor host driver (vendor_host.c/.h) and the KHCI device driver were removed (ci_fs replaces it); the audit fixes themselves remove no API, but hosts now reject more malformed devices (bad CSW, truncated CDC and hub descriptors, isochronous or control CDC notification endpoints) and RUSB2 init fails on an unsupported PHY crystal instead of hanging. The ci_fs NAK toggle fix was reverted after hardware showed it broke MSC mount on Kinetis and is reopened; deferred work is in 20 grouped follow-up issues, low and nit items in a separate PR. Rebased onto master 93aa62bce after master took 229 more commits (218 to 490eb4ec9, then PR 4594 and PRs 4592/4593): of the 73 findings this PR lists, 62 stay fixed by its commits, 7 were fixed on master by PRs 4517, 4544 and 4593 and their audit commits were dropped or folded, one stays reverted (ci_fs NAK toggle, issue 4533), one is superseded by master requiring power-of-two stream packets and two were dropped by the owner. The new master range raised no defect in the audit commits; master defects went to issues 4598, 4601, 4605 and 4606 and comments on existing ones. The dwc2 abort-retire ChHltd write was dropped because it made an ESP32-S3 host MSC hang that master also shows (issue 4605) more frequent; the released-channel finding stays fixed by the HAINT&HAINTMSK gate.

claims.claim: Standard GET_DESCRIPTOR, GET_CONFIGURATION, GET_INTERFACE and GET_STATUS are device-to-host only, and an undefined or invalid standard request is a Request Error answered with STALL.
Wrong wValue, wIndex or wLength on GET_CONFIGURATION, GET_INTERFACE or GET_STATUS is unspecified behaviour, so STALL is allowed but not required.
A device without a Default Control Pipe Halt feature may answer SET/CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT) on endpoint 0 with a Request Error, and must do so for a non-existent endpoint.
Full-speed bulk wMaxPacketSize is limited to 8, 16, 32 or 64 and high-speed bulk to 512, while interrupt and isochronous sizes have no power-of-two rule.
Periodic bInterval ranges and wMaxPacketSize bits 12..11 additional transactions are as Table 9-13 specifies.
With wMaxPacketSize bits 12..11 at 01 or 10 the per-transaction size must be 513-1024 or 683-1024, so two transactions of 512 bytes is invalid.
USB 2.0 permits polling an interrupt endpoint more slowly than its bInterval, as the DWC2 low-speed clamp comment states.
Data toggle is unchanged across a NAK, so a retried transaction reuses the same data PID.
A receiver that sees a data PID mismatch ACKs and discards the packet as a duplicate without toggling.
An OUT transaction can send its DATA packet and then receive NAK, unlike an IN NAK which carries no data packet.
Non-control endpoint toggles reset to DATA0 only on SetConfiguration, SetInterface or ClearFeature(ENDPOINT_HALT), and ClearFeature(ENDPOINT_HALT) resets it even on an unhalted endpoint.
A device applies a new address only after the SET_ADDRESS status stage completes.
bMaxPower is in 2 mA units and a configuration may draw at most five unit loads (500 mA), so a 510 mA clamp exceeds the limit.
A control IN data stage may end early on a short or zero-length packet, so the actual received length must be used.
A descriptor shorter than its defined size is rejected, and an extended descriptor is traversed by its bLength, ignoring extra bytes.
Low-speed devices receive no SOF packets.
Hub descriptor field offsets are bNbrPorts at 2 and bPwrOn2PwrGood at 5.
Required hub descriptor bytes, accepted port-count bounds, and which enumeration requests may fail without abandoning enumeration, are pending.
Required bus reset assertion, recovery and debounce intervals, and whether i.MX RT reset self-terminates near 55 ms so the wait can be relocated per HCD, are pending.
